citation_note: Logs in A and B are unnumbered, so their citations use 1-based entry order (#n). C and D cite their own `n` fields. Severity is judged for a disposable simulated ledger: over-refunds mean ledger-integrity and business-rule breaches, not real-money loss. Severity and discoverability ratings are my assessments, not the reporters' labels.

R1_cumulative_over_refund.evidence: #1 shows A200 refunded=0. #4 refunds 5000 (200, refunded 5000). #5 repeats it (200, refunded 10000). #6 GET confirms 10000 against paid 6000.
R1_cumulative_over_refund.severity: High (ledger-integrity rule broken; the report's 'money loss' framing overstates a simulated ledger)
R1_cumulative_over_refund.discoverability: High: two identical partial refunds, deterministic

R2_stale_address_overwrite.evidence: #6 shows v1. #7 saves 'Newer Addr' at v1 (200, v2). #8 saves 'Stale Addr' at v1 (200, v3). #9 GET shows the stale value.
R2_stale_address_overwrite.discoverability: High: reuse a previously read version

R3_partial_batch_change.status: actionable (defect shown), but the per-path claim is incomplete
R3_partial_batch_change.evidence: #1 shows A100 standard. #10 [A100,B100] returned 403. #11 [A100,ZZZ] returned 404. A100 was read only after both calls (#12: express). B100 unchanged (#13).
R3_partial_batch_change.gap: Both failing calls targeted A100 with no read in between. The log proves at least one rejected call mutated A100, but not which one (403 path or 404 path).
R3_partial_batch_change.severity: Medium-High (a rejected call leaves the caller's own orders changed; no cross-user write)
R3_partial_batch_change.discoverability: Moderate: needs a mixed batch with the owned ID listed before the bad ID

limitations: The assessment uses only each report and its retained logs. Source code, probe scripts, outputs and D's restore file were not available, so code-cause claims and test-coverage claims are unverified. A's and C's logs are partly truncated. A and B have no probe numbers. No case tested R3 with the bad ID listed first, so its order dependence is inferred from the reports' code reading. The severity and discoverability ratings are judgements, not measurements.
